sentence: Apixaban is an anticoagulant, a medicine that helps prevent blood clots from forming.
note: NHS: medicine used to prevent blood clots; anticoagulant.

sentence: It is available in the UK only on prescription.
note: Search summary of NHS page: only available on prescription.

sentence: The NHS lists uses such as lowering the chance of a stroke in people with an irregular heartbeat, and treating or preventing clots in the veins and lungs.
note: NHS About apixaban (via search summary and existing page entry); wording of the exact list not shown in this search, kept general.

sentence: Apixaban makes the blood take longer to clot, which lowers the chance of a harmful clot but also means bleeding can last longer.
note: NHS: prevents blood clots; the link to longer bleeding is from the NHS side-effect list (bleeding more easily). Mechanism wording is a textbook statement.

sentence: The tablets can be taken with or without food.
note: Search summary of NHS How and when to take: with or without food.

sentence: Taking it at the same time each day is the usual advice, and missed tablets matter, so the NHS page on missed doses is worth reading for what to do.
note: Search summary: same time every day; missed-dose rules and do not take two to make up.

sentence: The NHS says a person should not stop apixaban without talking to their doctor.
note: Search summary: do not stop taking apixaban without talking to your doctor.

sentence: The most common side effect is bleeding more easily than normal.
note: NHS: most common side effect is bleeding more easily.

sentence: This can show as nosebleeds, bleeding gums, bruising or heavier periods.
note: NHS side effects page list.

sentence: The NHS says this kind of minor bleeding is not dangerous and usually stops on its own, but it should be mentioned to the doctor if it is bothersome or does not stop.
note: Search summary of NHS: minor bleeding not dangerous, usually stops by itself; tell doctor if it bothers you or does not stop.

sentence: For red or black poo, or bruises that appear for no reason or keep growing, the NHS advice is to contact NHS 111.
note: NHS side effects page: 111 for red pee or black poo or unexplained/growing bruises.

sentence: For a nosebleed that lasts a long time despite pressure, blood in vomit, coughing up blood, or bleeding from a cut or injury that will not slow down, the NHS advice is to go to A&E.
note: NHS side effects page: A&E list.

sentence: For signs of bleeding in the brain, such as a sudden severe headache, fits, sudden vision changes or numbness, the NHS says to call 999 or go to A&E.
note: Search summary: 999 or A&E for possible brain bleeding; ask someone to drive or call ambulance.

sentence: A serious allergic reaction, such as swelling of the face or difficulty breathing, is a reason to call 999.
note: Search summary: serious allergic reaction, call 999.

sentence: A few medicines interact with apixaban, so prescribers need to know about everything a person takes, including over-the-counter medicines, vitamins and herbal supplements.
note: Search summary: tell prescribers about all medicines incl. OTC, vitamins, herbal supplements.

sentence: Some antidepressants and painkillers are among those that can cause problems alongside it.
note: Search summary: one source notes some antidepressants or painkillers can cause problems.

sentence: The NHS says drinking alcohol is possible while on apixaban.
note: Search summary: NHS says you can drink alcohol.

sentence: Heavy or binge drinking can increase the effect of apixaban and make bleeding more likely.
note: Search summary of NHS: heavy drinking especially binge drinking increases the effect and bleeding risk.

sentence: People on apixaban are given an anticoagulant alert card by their doctor or pharmacist.

sentence: The advice is to carry it at all times and show it to a doctor or dentist before surgery or dental treatment.

sentence: Apixaban may need to be paused for a period before a planned operation, dental or medical procedure, and the clinical team decides this.

sentence: Apixaban is not suitable for people who have had an allergic reaction to it or another anticoagulant.
